assembly_instructions: Conceptual architecture diagram of the Ethereum protocol, rendered as a city at 1x scale (bounds radius ~8.9 m, no scaling needed). Step 1: cast the ground-level EXECUTION LAYER floor slab (concrete, 13x8 m, top at y=0.3) and ring it with four perimeter concrete curbs — the root of the assembly. Step 2: pour four concrete pile-cap footings on the ground behind the slab at x=+/-4.5, z=4.3 and z=6.9, and stand a 3.85 m welded-steel support pillar on each footing. Step 3: tie the four pillar tops together with a perimeter ring-beam of four welded-steel cross-ties and run two welded-steel joists across the deck underside so the upper deck is fully framed, not floating. Step 4: set the raised CONSENSUS LAYER floor slab (10x3.4 m) on the braced pillars and joists at y=4.0 and ring it with four perimeter curbs. Step 5: on the execution slab lay the concrete ledger foundation and stand a row of six glass 'block' buildings of varying height, linked block-to-block by five copper hash links; build the dark mempool holding yard front-left as a floor plate with three perimeter walls (front, left, right) left open toward the viewer, holding three glass pending-transaction cubes; place three white smart-contract buildings front-right and a black RPC/gateway tower at the +X edge tied to the head block by a copper bus. Step 6: stand the Ethereum diamond monument (concrete plinth + lower inverted glass cone + upper glass cone) at the front-centre edge of the execution slab as the city landmark. Step 7: on the consensus deck run a copper Beacon Chain spine down the centre and cluster eight tapered brushed-steel validator towers in two rows of four flanking the spine, ring each tower base with a copper staked-ETH token and cap each with a copper attestation beacon. Step 8: run the vertical copper Engine-API riser from the execution slab up through the consensus deck and join it to the Beacon Chain spine with a short horizontal copper Engine-API link; finally install the inclined access stair with its two stringers from the execution slab up to the consensus deck front edge. View from a raised 3/4 angle so every block, validator and district reads clearly.

info.japanese_name: イーサリアム（都市メタファー）
info.summary: Ethereum is a decentralized, proof-of-stake blockchain and global compute platform; here its architecture is drawn as a city with execution and consensus districts. Each visual block is a real network block, each tower a validator staking 32 ETH.
info.description: Ethereum launched on 30 July 2015 as a programmable blockchain running the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). Since The Merge on 15 September 2022 it secures itself with proof-of-stake: an execution layer (which orders transactions, runs the EVM and holds account state) and a consensus layer (the Beacon Chain, which selects block proposers and finalizes blocks) operate as paired but distinct subsystems. The model splits these into two stacked districts.
info.description_2: Blocks are produced once per 12-second slot, with 32 slots per 6.4-minute epoch. A validator must stake 32 ETH; roughly one million validators are active. Transactions wait in the mempool before inclusion, smart contracts are autonomous on-chain programs, and RPC/gateway nodes expose the network to applications — all represented here as named city districts wired together by copper buses.
info.operator: Ethereum Foundation and a decentralized global community of node operators
info.contractor: Ethereum core developer teams (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus)
